name: MathlibAnnex.Piola.cofactorRow
title: A cofactor row by row replacement

content.display_title: A cofactor row by row replacement
content.one_sentence_role: Fixes the cofactor convention used in the divergence and determinant identities.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A=(A_{kq})$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix, and fix a row index $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Write $e_j=(\delta_{jq})_{q=1}^n$ for the $j$th coordinate vector. The cofactor row $C_i(A)$ is the vector whose $j$th coordinate is the determinant obtained by replacing row $i$ of $A$ by $e_j^{\mathsf T}$.
content.definition_explanation:
For a row vector $v$, let $A[i\leftarrow v]$ denote $A$ with only its $i$th row replaced by $v$. Then
$$C_i(A)=\bigl(C_i(A)_j\bigr)_{j=1}^n,\qquad
C_i(A)_j=\det\bigl(A[i\leftarrow e_j^{\mathsf T}]\bigr).$$
Equivalently, $C_i(A)_j$ is the usual $(i,j)$ cofactor. The row-replacement formula fixes the row and column convention without choosing an inverse.
content.assumptions: The matrix is arbitrary: invertibility is not required. The dimension is a natural number, with a specified $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. When $n=0$ there is no such index, so this indexed definition has no instance to evaluate.
content.conclusion: The result is a row in $\mathbb R^n$, using the row convention throughout. No transpose or choice of an inverse is part of the definition.
content.lean_realization_notes: The later row-expansion lemma gives $\det(A[i\leftarrow v])=\sum_jv_jC_i(A)_j$. It is cited as a separate identity, not included as an additional conclusion of this definition.
